correctness.rationale: Exact all-n eigenspace decomposition using unsigned K_n incidence and PBH gives the lower bound and the odd-unicyclic submatrix criterion. A separate, complete connected/disconnected and parity analysis of the complementary controlled-edge graph isolates only n=6, K3+K3. A formal labeled-cycle EGF counts all choices. The independent stdlib rational-rank verifier checks all 252 cases for n=5 and all 5005 for n=6, deterministic n=7 rank samples, all 116280 n=7 subsets structurally, and rational series coefficients, without substituting enumeration for infinite proof.

evidence: Monshizadeh–Zhang–Camlibel prove a family-of-matrices result, with universal qualitative-class quantification.
Brešar–Kos–Torres prove Z(KG(n,2))=N-6 for n>=7, while the new fixed-Laplacian minimum is N-n, strictly smaller.
Yazicioglu–Abbas–Egerstedt provide graph-distance lower bounds rather than the complete fixed Kneser classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A stronger graph-generic result would have to imply the sharp fixed-matrix cardinality AND iff placement criterion for every n>=5. Qualitative-class zero forcing is not equivalent for a single prescribed Laplacian, and the stronger-zero-forcing necessary implication fails numerically for n>=7. The checked distance and minimum-leader frameworks do not supply the sharp Kneser incidence/eigenspace equivalence.

Strong structural/zero-forcing results apply to a qualitative family, not to this fixed matrix; the published Kneser zero-forcing number N-6 for n>=7 is strictly larger than N-n. The known unsigned incidence lemma and Kneser eigenvalues are credited; the new combination is the precise PBH unactuated pseudoforest correspondence plus six-label exception, minimum and enumeration.

value.rationale: This is an all-parameter natural infinite-family actuator placement classification in control theory, resolving the minimal number and every placement via an easily tested odd-unicyclic complement criterion, plus an actual spectral balanced-partition exception for n=6 and exact exponential-generating enumeration. For n>=7 the optimum strictly improves over the known robust zero-forcing sufficient size, a mathematically motivated gap between fixed and qualitative-class control, not a routine numerical table.
